Hangman and accessible letter entry on NoCharge

How current Hangman accepts alphabet-button guesses or page-level A–Z key presses, announces guess results, and handles six misses without a timer.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Guess the calm word, one letter at a time.

Play HangmanBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: Current Hangman accepts guesses from labeled A–Z buttons or physical letter keys while the round is active. Its live status reports each guess; the word pattern also has an accessible text label.

Two ways to enter a letter

  • Buttons: Activate one of the 26 letter buttons with a pointer, touch, Enter, or Space.
  • Physical keyboard: Press an A–Z key while focus is not in a text input or textarea. The game ignores modifier-key combinations, key repeats, non-letter keys, and letters already guessed.

A physical key press submits a guess; it does not move focus to the corresponding letter button. Repeated guesses do not add another miss.

How the current state is announced

The live status line says whether the guessed letter is in the word and reports the round result when it ends. The word row exposes an accessible name containing the revealed letters and blank positions, and the interface separately shows the missed letters, total mistakes, and word length. The row itself is not a live region, so do not assume every visual change is automatically announced.

Six misses, no clock

The game ends when the word is solved or six distinct incorrect letters have been used. There is no per-guess timer or speed score. The current word list is a short fixed list in the module; it is not an external dictionary.

This describes the visible controls and labels in the current source. It is not a certification for every browser, screen reader, keyboard layout, or assistive-technology setup. Test the live page with the input method you use.
